_comment: Substrate in-app tests (text-adventure wrapper + flash + runner + jta + omsi + maze consumable tiles). Runs under the full module config (modules.json) so the substrate runtimes register — unlike test-regression, which uses modules-nograph.json and therefore cannot load them. New substrate tests must be added here (they register enabled:false so they don't leak into other modes).

tests._comment: Former KNOWN-RED stray-append diagnostic — green since the M3b coarse-capture refactor retired loop-mode end-appends (CC/docs/plans/loops-coarse-capture-plan.md).

M6 slice 5c: the summary Bot economy leg. Replaces the deleted scripts/procgen/verify-bounce-loop-mode.mjs (whose premise — auto walkTo with no mode system — is obsolete, and which rotted red for months because nothing gate-ran it). A Bot block hands the queued regionMove to the walkTo solver; the auto-runner plays the flat level on real physics and the pool falls by the per-second TIME drain, not per-action defaults.

The deterministic leg for the reset-authority fix (2026-07-24): the energy pin DECLINES while the fork is latched, and the bridge reports the run end so the host — the sole reset authority — fires the loop reset. Builds the divergence directly (latched at 0 with mana still in the pool, so no drain can ever arrive) and folds setEnergy mutations rather than polling, because the reset erases the state within a beat. Its companion oracle is the bridge's 'breaking a latched energy reset' warning: with this fix that circuit breaker must never fire across a run batch.

M6: restructured onto the Bot radio and re-enabled. It no longer calls walkTo directly with a hand-rolled reset-retry loop — it parks a BOT block and lets the real queue machinery drive, so the gate exemption, the multi-reset walk, and the fine-substrate economy are under test rather than emulated. The former leg 2 (synthetic exit-task id stability) is now jta-synthetic-exit-task-id-stability.

RE-ENABLED 2026-07-25 (post-D2 cleanup). Its old KNOWN-RED note carried a diagnosis that was WRONG — kept here refuted rather than deleted. That note blamed loadRegion for calling _applyCatchUpResets() BEFORE reading `const completed = _completedThisLoop.has(regionId)`. The ordering is CORRECT: a loop reset genuinely un-plays the zone (doAnyReset rebuilds it) and loadZone({completed:true}) marks every task reps=max_reps FOR FREE, so honoring a pre-reset completion would grant back a zone the reset just took away. The prescribed reorder was also inert — the gameState:loopReset subscriber bumps _hostResetCount and CLEARS _completedThisLoop in the same handler, so a pending catch-up delta always arrives with an already-cleared set (bridge.js now carries a warn-level tripwire in case a refactor ever splits those two). The real defect was this test's own prep: it only pumped ticks, and managed zone play has NO automation unless something arms it (_armWalkAutomation, on a walk), so the zone never completed and the first assertion could never pass. The prep now plays zone 0 with explicit performTask calls, Travel LAST (the fork disables Travel while a Mandatory task is unfinished, and this zone's single exit is item-gated on a perk one of its own tasks awards). A final leg pins the reset semantics the old flake misread. Full ruling: docs/json/developer/procgen/jta.md.

RE-ENABLED in M6 slice 5 after an empirical check: this test contains NO walkTo at all. It enters the region with the synthetic-move-exempt moveToRegion helper and then makes pure settings/pool assertions, so the M3b strict gate was never in its way. Its old deferral note ("drives zone 0 via PlaybackController.walkTo") described a different test — it was swept into M4's bulk deferral of the four jta walkTo tests. Verified green at HEAD before any M6 slice-5 change touched it.

Randomized+balanced 4-zone progression. MECHANISM (as-written): drives cross-region zone progression with a direct unparked PlaybackController.walkTo (walkOneZone). Since M4 opted jta into the M3b strict action gate, the bridge's fromLoop-less walkTo departure is gate-blocked with no parked block, so the test is NOT runnable on demand in its current form. REVIVAL PATH: restructure each zone leg onto a Bot block (the M6 wake fix, slice 5d, removed the blocker that made this impossible — a fork-propagated reset teleport no longer hard-pauses a bot park; it releases and re-drives). WHY NOT IN-SUITE YET: the normal-ticking runtime wall. These are balance/dataset VALIDATION tests that must run at normal ticking — Instant is affordability-blind (completeTaskInstantly finishes tasks whatever the solved cost, so the test would pass on a wedged world; see jtaBalanceTests.js:173), so a full multi-zone playthrough compounding skills across resets exceeds a practical gate-run budget (240s/zone x multiple legs did not converge in-suite). STATUS: DEFERRED, tracked in the fable->opus handoff queue doc. jta-bot-walkto-exit is the real Bot in-app leg; this test's UNIQUE strata (shuffle non-vacuity, cold balance solve at rules load, AP-authoritative perk accounting) are what it exists for.

M4 fine-grained record→playback round trip across a zone boundary — jta's in-app progression stratum while the four walkTo progression tests stay KNOWN-DEFERRED to M6. Also carries the folded-in energyBonusSync assertion from jta-starting-energy-bonus-raises-pool.

Region-atlas Phase 5b. The Phase-4 flash flavour of the same atlas can only be a SKIP-able standalone verifier (it needs a gitignored 31 MB wasm artifact); the maze projection of the same geometry runs from the committed repo, which is why these two legs can be enumerated here at all. No batch claims this category, so it rides the default `fast` batch.
Region-atlas Phase 6. Same map, but walked in a world sphere growth GREW: the leg that catches an arrival landing inside a wall, which no compile or sphere oracle can.

Region-atlas Phase 8 slice B. The SHIPPED playback bot beats the grown world end to end; the headless witness (atlasMazeBot.slow.test.js) proves the same world beatable by walking tiles directly, so the two strata are independent.
APWorld hub H1. The Document tab is DERIVED from rules.schema.json; this row fetches the schema at run time and asserts the drawn key set EQUALS the declared one, both directions.
APWorld hub H1. One set-key through the real change event, then the panel's own Undo: the fold over the shorter list is what catches an op that stored the caller's object instead of a copy.
APWorld hub H1. The Links tab's substrate rows are derived from the live substrateRegistry's roomEditor declarations; the expected set is read off the registry in the browser, never listed here.

APWorld hub H2. The button the ⚖ asked for on the opened-preset screen. It only RAISES the hub (ui:activatePanel) — the preset load already published the document app-wide — so the assertion is that the hub's session names the same game and seed, read off the loaded document.

APWorld hub H2. Intercepts URL.createObjectURL and asserts the BLOB's bytes, not that a file appeared: a page-initiated download is inert in some sandboxes. A working-copy edit must be in those bytes, which a download reading applied state would fail.

APWorld hub H2. Apply published 'apworldEditorApply', which sphereState can neither parse as a preset path nor recognise as one of its four in-memory sources, so it reset the sphere state and loaded nothing for 199 of 205 presets. This row opens a FILE-LOGGED preset, applies, and asserts the log survived.

APWorld hub H2b. The raw tab mounts CodeMirror 6 (editable, whole working copy, the shared extension list's line numbers and fold gutter, no textarea left) and Save JSON writes ONE replace-document op carrying a PARSED OBJECT that one undo folds away byte for byte. H2's size-guard cases are gone with the guard; the largest-preset case moved to its own row.

APWorld hub H2b, B-c's undo rule over a widget that is not an <input>. The hub's key handler refuses Ctrl+Z inside anything isContentEditable — a clause that had never had a contenteditable widget under it until CM6 mounted here. Drives BOTH halves: inside the editor the session must not move, on the panel chrome the same keystroke must pop it.

APWorld hub H2b. stardew_valley is 2,620,221 pretty bytes — above H2's RAW_VIEW_LIMIT_BYTES = 2,000,000, so at H2 the tab showed it a refusal screen. The row asserts that premise off the document, then that the view holds the WHOLE document to the character: a virtualised editor draws only the visible lines, so a truncated string would look identical on screen.

APWorld hub H3. The Map tab's canvas is compared against what the document's own preset_sidecars say — region count and grid dimensions derived at run time, never typed — and then a drawn cell's PIXEL is sampled, because a renderer that threw after sizing the canvas would leave every dimension check green.

APWorld hub H3, plan §3 idea 4. The click→cell mapping is the renderer's exported geometry, the same one the pipeline's hit-tester uses; the row clicks the first placed cell's centre and asserts EXACTLY one region block is marked selected in the Regions tab, then that a click off the grid moves nothing.

APWorld hub H3, ⚖ 'show the composite grid only for presets that have grid data'. Loads a committed jta preset (one of the 4 of 205 whose sidecars carry no grid_cell), asserts that premise off the document, and then that the tab names the reason and draws NO canvas — the region graph stays its own panel rather than a fallback drawn here.

APWorld hub H4a. The four-player fixture's first row: the combined export (no playerId) opens on the first slot and offers exactly the slots the document carries; the per-player P3 export (playerId "3") opens on 3. One document alone cannot tell 'honour playerId' from 'take the first slot' — this row drives both.

APWorld hub H4a. One document, four slots, two games: the maze slots draw a canvas holding THAT slot's region count, the bounce slots say 'no map for this world' and draw none (⚖ 3's v1 answer, now on the same document as a slot that draws). Switches back at the end — a map that never re-derived passes the walk in order.

APWorld hub H4a. The Document tab's per-player slice, finally observable: 158 of 192 carriers held {} and every populated one keyed under slot '1', so no committed document could discriminate. The fixture's slots hold 3/3/5/5, and the row asserts the four summaries are not all the same string.

APWorld hub H4b. Three shapes of answer on two documents: a sidecar-bearing region offers its room, a sidecar-less one draws NO button (an absence, not a disabled control), a substrate with no roomEditor (jta) is disabled without being pressed, and a region whose payload does not round-trip is disabled only AFTER the press — the expensive half of the check deserializes a world, so it runs on demand. H6b moved that case: it used to be the fixture's slot-3 region_1_1 (its spring_gap level's north portal is authored as exit_up and the bounce re-assembly minted side_exit_<side> for every exit), but H6b made the assembler read the level's own portal ids, the bounce door went 15/25 to 25/25 over the committed corpus, and slot 3 now asserts the opposite. The press-then-refuse arm drives a seedling_atlas_maze room instead - the ten rooms written by the atlas derivation rather than serializeMazeWorld, which is the refusal that remains (H6a's to fix). A Seedling region is the fourth shape — its substrate HAS a room editor and declares regionRoundTrip: {refused}, so the title is the substrate's OWN sentence about its payload. Driving that is what kills the mutant that ignores the declaration: without it the button-side use of regionRoundTripOf was uncovered and the mutant stayed green.

APWorld hub H4b. The lab door end to end without an iframe: the host is a PANEL-SHAPED stub (W4's own contract shape, the same one createPageLabTransport implements) and the three phases of labRoomEditor's contract are published on procgenLab:levelChanged. The first version mounted the real maze lab; the page connected inside the row's own poll, opened room 0 for real and published its OWN close, so onSave fired with the page's UNEDITED record and the row measured a no-op — a live page and a synthetic one cannot both author the same conversation. Asserts the handed document is a ONE-ENTRY region library, the navigate asks for ?source=set&room=0, the close returns exactly ONE hub op moving payload AND the one rule the door proved it authored, the exit targets and baked AP location names the library capture strips are restored, and ONE Undo folds it all away.

APWorld hub H4c. The reverse link that needs no protocol: the bounce region editor and the hub are panels in ONE app, so the door names a region and raises the hub, carrying no document at all (the level in that panel is a working copy nobody saved back). Driven through the bounce module's OWN publisher, not a hand-written publish — the button and the hub's subscriber only meet there. Four answers, not one claim four times: a region of the slot the hub is showing is selected and its block marked; a region no slot holds is SAID SO rather than switching to a tab with nothing highlighted; a named slot the document has moves the selector FIRST and then selects (through _chosenPlayer, because _syncPlayer re-derives playerId on every render and would otherwise undo the move inside the door's own re-render); and a slot the document does not have is refused by name with the hub staying where it was.

APWorld hub H5. Two measurements meet here. (1) The region_atlas block in a rules.json is a REFERENCE ({atlas_id, game, map_document}) and never an atlas — all three committed carriers — and nothing resolves an atlas id back to its file. (2) module-configs/modules.json disables regionMarkingTool in the DEFAULT mode, so the door would publish ui:activatePanel into a warn-and-return: the first shape of this row waited 8 s for a panel that cannot exist and reported STARVED. The button is therefore SHOWN, DISABLED, with the panel and the config file in its title, while still printing what a save WOULD come back as. The end-to-end save lives in check-region-marking-tool.mjs, under ?mode=flash.

APWorld hub H5. procgenPipeline:loadRules is a SECOND channel beside stateManager:rawJsonDataLoaded on purpose: one means 'the app loaded this', the other 'here is a document nobody applied'. The row asserts the pipeline adopted the hand-off, named the door, and QUOTED the engine's own refusal — read from sphereRebuildRefusal at run time, never typed. Measured: procgen_maze/AP_1 is grid-growth with no sphere tree, so its answer is TOP-DOWN, not 'append a sphere'.

APWorld hub H5. Plan §4 priced this link as 'Apply, then open' because the cost debugger reads applied state; the measurement overturned it — CostPlanner takes its state manager as a constructor argument and touches it through two methods, so a rules.json can wear that face via StateManager.loadFromJSON (4 ms to 306 ms across the corpus). The row asserts the debugger's status line says which world the numbers describe, and that there is a named way back.

Loop-costs L3. ⚖ (i) the walk prices EVERY region as coarse because that is how the numbers are derived; writeCostsByClass then drops the ones no block should carry. jta_schedule_test separates them: all three regions are NATIVE, so the block holds 1 of 4 regions and 0 of 23 locations while the plan behind it says 50/35/26 and 100/70/52. Before L3 the panel printed those as prices (cost=100 on a location the block does not price) and Verify scored the runtime 1/32 within tolerance for charging nothing, which was the design. Mutant: _pricingOf returning {priced:true} for NATIVE reds this row and nothing else.

Loop-costs L4. ⚖ (user, 2026-09-06) 'the debugger's plan comes back as ONE op'. Driven on omsi_substrate_test because that is the only shape where both halves are real: its committed block is EMPTY (all ten tracked carriers are), its two maze regions are coarse-classed so the block must gain their real prices (L3 measured 16 and 21 against a stored 50), and its omsi region is NATIVE so it must gain nothing. jta_schedule_test would have made 'it became priced' true of one zero. The row also drives the SCHEMA VETO at _acceptEditorOp — L4 measured it was not on the editor-op path at all (it lived in _applySetKey, the raw-JSON editor's method), so region_atlas's save had been bypassing it since H5. ⚠ The loop_costs schema is TYPE-only: it refuses a location cost that is not a number, and accepts every semantic error write-by-class is about (a moveCost on a summary region, a missing defaultRegionXpEffect, an entry for a native region) — reported, not fixed here.

Loop-costs R-a residue 3. ⚖ (user, 2026-09-06) 'take care of the residues'; L4 named the presence switch as an editor action and left it unbuilt. Driven on procgen_maze because it carries NO loop_costs block at all — the state the enable half is about, which none of the corpus's fourteen carriers can show — and its four regions make the post-enable readout a real '0 of 4' rather than '0 of 0'. The two undos are the claim: 'no key' and 'an empty block' are different document states, and a gesture that mutated rulesDoc in place would collapse them and still pass the first half.

Loop-costs R-a residue 2. L4 measured that onSave applied into whatever session the hub had open NOW — arc-wide, region_atlas's Save too — and could not close it without a document identity the hub did not carry. The hub now stamps a monotonic _documentToken at its ONE session boundary and _openDocumentKeyEditor binds it into the onSave closure, so no door can forget it. The SUBJECT here is the SECOND document: procgen_maze must still carry no loop_costs and its op list must not grow. A row that only read the debugger's status line would pass against a hub that printed a refusal and applied the op anyway.

APWorld hub H5. The ⚖ the Links tab exists for: 'even if the current rules.json file doesn't contain any relevant data for them'. On a document with no region_atlas the row must still be there, carry the REGISTRY's own label (the same string the Document tab shows, because both read DOCUMENT_KEY_EDITORS), say the document has nothing for it, and open the editor anyway.

APWorld coverage W0. Until W0 a tab-owned Document row drew 'edited in the X tab' and RETURNED, so every field of world except the one the Meta tab draws was reachable only through the whole-document Raw JSON editor — measured on stardew, where all fourteen owned rows offered neither a toggle nor an input. The subject is the RECORD, not the toggle: the row presses the block's own Save JSON and asserts ONE player-scope set-key on a sub-key no META_FIELDS spec addresses (derived from the Meta tab's own table), the Meta field beside it unmoved, and ONE undo taking the sub-key back out.

APWorld coverage S1, ⚖ (user, 2026-09-08) 'a "Sidecars" tab, for the data that's specifically in the sidecars'. Driven on procgen_maze, which carries procgen_metadata and three per-region sidecars in slot 1. Asserts the tab draws exactly the keys KEYS_OWNED_BY_TAB.sidecars names, in registry order; that preset_sidecars is a one-line per-slot SUMMARY counted off the document with a button whose EFFECT is the Regions tab; that a key's box on this tab is element-for-element the box the Document tab builds for it (one renderer, two hosts — a forked renderer that happened to draw a door and a block would still differ); and that the Document rows for the five gained the Sidecars pointer WITHOUT losing their own affordance. ⛔ This row reads the SAME table the tab filters by, so it is blind to a key REMOVED from that table — the membership is guarded in documentKeys.test.js, whose population comes from the exporter's own _inject_worldgen_* methods and from the ⚖.

APWorld coverage R1, ⚖ (user, 2026-09-09) 'The sidecar entries in the sidecars tab have the Go to Sidecars button. Is there a simple way to fix that?' S1 gave the Sidecars tab the Document tab's row renderer and the 'Edited in the X tab' pointer came with it. The population is the LAW's — every key KEYS_OWNED_BY_TAB files under the Sidecars tab — and the CONTROL is the other host: absent on its own tab (while keeping its editing affordance, so a renderer that skipped the whole owned branch again would not pass), present on the Document tab with a button whose EFFECT is the Sidecars tab, and a key owned by a THIRD tab still pointing. That last row is what separates 'the host suppresses its own pointer' from 'the pointer is gone'.

APWorld coverage R1, S1 §8.6 (2) — S1 shipped the accepted-op focus UNCONDITIONAL, which is a claim about every editor at once: the cost debugger's Send ENDS the visit, but the region marking tool is a workspace whose Save is a checkpoint. ⛔ _acceptEditorOp is driven DIRECTLY because region_atlas's panel is disabled in the default mode, so no gesture here reaches the seam — the op's value comes from the schema's own `required` list, so the veto on the accepted path is real. The non-vacuity is inside the row: accepted + applied + the beside-the-row sentence recorded (the half focusHubOnSave does NOT gate) before the no-raise claims, because 'the hub did not come forward' is also true of a seam that refused or never ran. The `true` half is apworld-loop-costs-send-writes-the-plan-as-one-op, so a mutant that ignores the flag reds one row whichever way it is wired.

APWorld coverage W0, ⚖ (user, 2026-09-08) 'we could link to the existing dungeons and helpers panels as viewers'. Both halves come from an authority rather than a string: whether the door is offered is asked of centralRegistry.getAllPanelComponents() — the same set the hub's own _panelRefusal consults — and whether the press worked is panelManager.isPanelActive, the panel actually in front. region_atlas is asserted ABSENT from that same set, so 'registered' discriminates instead of describing a mode where everything is on.

APWorld coverage W3, ⚖ (user, 2026-09-08) 'Yes, canonical placements should have their own tab.' Every count is DERIVED from the fetched document rather than typed, so the row cannot pass by agreeing with the panel. It also asserts the option list is LAZY — a closed select carries only the blank option and its own value — because a select per location carrying every item is 1,442,352 elements on dark_souls_3, the largest committed world.

APWorld coverage W3. Both halves are driven because only one of them can make each claim: on procgen_topdown/AP_1 every location is already placed, so a REPLACE is one op that moves the value and moves NEITHER readout, and only the blank '(unplaced)' option moves the tab's summary and the Document row's { n keys }. The op's own refusals are guarded in rulesDocOps.test.js, not here.

APWorld coverage W3, on the four-player multiworld fixture. ⛔ The brief said slot 1's block is ABSENT there; measured, it is PRESENT and empty ({}), and slots 3 and 4 carry six placements each — so the law driven is that a slot-3 op leaves slot 1's block byte-identical, whatever it holds. Mutant: reading placements from slot '1' instead of the selected slot reds this row.

APWorld coverage W3 — the requirement no other row can see. The schema declares the placement slot additionalProperties: true, so a stale entry validates and no committed preset carries one; this row hands the hub a committed preset with two added on the way in through stateManager:rawJsonDataLoaded, which is what a hand-edited file is. It is also why set-canonical-placement does not validate a DELETE.
